description: A correlated reference whose alias-qualified name collides with a column of the INNER table: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stage t WHERE t.id = s.id) where BOTH tables have an id. The subquery's outer-row context was keyed only by TABLE name (SRC.ID), so the alias-qualified s.id missed it and the strip-qualifier fallback bound it to the inner table's own column - turning the correlation into t.id = t.id, always true: EXISTS matched every outer row, NOT EXISTS none, and the ubiquitous dedup-guarded INSERT either inserted nothing or, where the guard erred the other way, inserted duplicates. Proper SQL scoping is preserved in the other direction too: with NO qualifier, a bare id really is the INNER table's column. Also covers a SELECT-list alias referenced in a JOIN's ON condition, which failed to resolve and silently matched no rows, and its mirror - a REAL column of the same name must win over such an alias. Converted 1:1 from query/CorrelatedExistsShadowTest (now retired).
